newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares close firmer, electronics rise.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares close firmer, electronics rise.

text.p: Singapore shares closed broadly firmer on Wednesday with investors snapping up electronics shares.
Leading the gainers were electronic stocks like Sunright, Uraco and Omni Industries, rising 7.5 to 0.00 percent in active trading of more than one million shares each.
This pushed the SES Electronics index up 1.42 percent to 101.64. ING Barings had called for a buy on Sunright and put its target price at S$2.00.
"We are still taking the cue from the U.S. and technololgy issues did well in the last session," said one broker.

Sentiment in the broader market was also upbeat, especially in the afternoon session, dealers said. The Straits Times Industrial index ended 16.57 points higher at 2,104.71 while the UOB OTC index rose 8.17 points to 1,226.37.
Total market volume was 152.32 million with 305 gainers thumping 64 losers.

NatSteel closed 12 cents higher at a new 1997 high of S$3.74 with more than 3.5 million shares traded. A dealer said funds were buying the company as it had a good recovery story. Fraser & Neave, Cycle & Carriage and Creative ended slighty lower.
